correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the positive Sturm–Liouville quadratic form, Neumann endpoints, interface continuity and delta-sink jump. At a fixed trial positive eigenvalue below each side mixed eigenvalue, logarithmic impedances ell and m increase/decrease with trap x, so ell+m is uniquely minimized at ell=m. Strict eigenvalue-impedance monotonicity converts that to unique global maximizing location. With k=2z/L, the slower segment has phase kx and the fast half gives right input phase alpha_r(z)=arctan(sqrt(r)tan(z/sqrt(r))), yielding kx=k(L/2-x)+alpha, the formula for x* and strength. alpha<z and alpha/z decreases strictly in z for r>1; z increases with kappa, giving x* decreasing from L/2 to pi L/(4z_inf). As r->infinity, z_inf->t0 solving tan t0=-t0; bound pi/(4t0)=0.38713253 sharp. Inspected transfer-matrix checker source and independent_checks.py verifies eigenvalue relation and competing positions for sample parameters; finite samples are not universal proof.
residual_risks: Statement depends on equal halves, positive piecewise-constant Fickian diffusion, a single positive delta absorber and Neumann endpoints.
Optimality proof relies on positivity of trial ground eigenfunction, correct impedance domain and monotonicity; tests cannot certify all continuous parameters.

originality.rationale: General diffusion and trap optimization is prior, but the inspected heterogeneous search papers address stochastic interpretation or weak-trap/small-target asymptotics, and the original multi-trap principal-eigenvalue papers differ in geometry. None inspected has the all-reactivity one-dimensional two-layer unique optimum or contrast-independent sharp displacement limit.

No conclusion extends to unequal layer lengths or nonlinear target functionals.
